match.reason: No bank point teaches China's shift from a mostly rural to a mostly urban country with its growth, pollution and crowding; the closest card, Internal migration in China, covers only the move of workers from villages to coastal cities and is narrower.

draft.title: Urbanisation in China
card: In 1980 most people in China lived in rural areas. Today most live in towns and cities. This change took only a few decades, which is very fast.
Factories were built in coastal cities such as Shenzhen and Shanghai. They offered jobs and higher wages than farming, so millions of rural people moved there for work.
The move helped the economy grow and raised the incomes of many families.
It also brought problems. Air pollution from factories and traffic, and crowded cities and housing, put pressure on people and services.
draft.remember: China urbanised fast as factory jobs drew rural people to coastal cities, with growth and pollution together.

a.q: Which best explains why millions of people in China moved to coastal cities?
opts: Factories there offered jobs and higher wages
The government closed all farms in rural areas
Coastal cities had far fewer people than villages
Rural areas had too much rain for any farming
a.why: Factories in coastal cities offered work that paid more than farming, so people were drawn there. The idea that all farms were closed is wrong: the card says people moved for jobs and wages.
a.clue: Think about what factories offered workers.

b.q: Mei leaves her family's village for a factory job in Shenzhen. Which problem is she most likely to find in the city?
opts: Air pollution and crowded housing
A shortage of jobs in factories
Lower wages than she earned farming
Fewer people than in her village
b.why: Fast city growth in China brought pollution and crowding. A shortage of factory jobs is wrong, because factories were the reason people moved to coastal cities.
b.clue: Think about what happens when many people and factories gather in one place.

a.best: Factories there offered jobs and higher wages

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about what factories offered workers' gives the answer away, because only one option mentions factories. A student can pick it without knowing the idea.
